suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-15 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. A nationally representative survey found most respondents with threshold and subthreshold bipolar spectrum disorder had lifetime comorbidity with other Axis I disorders, particularly anxiety disorders as a class; the approved relationship is limited to class-level population comorbidity association and does not establish onset order, direction, or individual causation. Require independently established bipolar disorder and a separately established anxiety disorder diagnosis; the cited nationally representative survey reported lifetime comorbidity of bipolar spectrum disorder with other Axis I disorders, particularly anxiety disorders as a class, and does not specify onset order or direction. Distinguish an independent anxiety disorder from anxiety symptoms occurring within manic, hypomanic, or depressive episodes. Preserve substance use, medical illness, medications, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Treat this only as population-level comorbidity association, not proof that bipolar disorder caused an individual's anxiety disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Lithium treatment in bipolar disorder carries a quantified, dose-related risk of hypothyroidism across three independent designs, while the risk is specific to lithium among the mood stabilisers and antipsychotics used for the same indication: the 2025 population-based retrospective cohort of incident bipolar disorder in Hong Kong (4,752 individuals with analysable hypothyroidism data, mean follow-up 8.4 years) reports lithium associated with increased hypothyroidism risk against non-lithium treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 2.00, 95 percent CI 1.72-2.33), with higher lithium serum levels associated with still greater risk (adjusted hazard ratio 2.08, 95 percent CI 1.67-2.59) and with valproate, olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone generally showing reduced likelihood of thyroid dysfunction compared with lithium, the same analysis deriving serum-level thresholds of approximately 0.50 mEq per litre for hypothyroidism, 0.50 for hyperthyroidism, and 0.59 for stage 3 or higher chronic kidney disease (PMID 39932712); the 2015 Oxford retrospective analysis of laboratory data over more than three decades reports that adjusting for age, sex, and diabetes, the presence of lithium in serum was associated with hypothyroidism (hazard ratio 2.31, 95 percent CI 2.05-2.60; p<0.0001) and with hypercalcaemia (1.43, 1.21-1.69) and stage 3 chronic kidney disease (1.93, 1.76-2.12) but NOT with hyperthyroidism (1.22, 95 percent CI 0.96-1.55; p=0.1010) or raised adjusted calcium (1.08, 0.88-1.34; p=0.4602), with women under 60 at greatest risk and higher-than-median lithium concentrations associated with increased risk of all adverse outcomes (PMID 26003379); and the 2016 competing-risk analysis of 24,574 US patients with bipolar disorder reports a four-year cumulative hypothyroidism risk of 8.8 percent on lithium against 6.3 percent on oxcarbazepine, the lowest-risk therapy, a 1.39-fold difference, while documenting that lithium was NOT statistically different from quetiapine, that hypothyroid risk error bars overlapped for all nine therapies, and that patients on lithium were tested for hypothyroidism 2.26 to 3.05 times more frequently than those on other treatments (PMID 27226264); recorded as documented association only with the treatment-mediated, detection-bias, and direction limits carried openly - this is an iatrogenic route in which the medication rather than the psychiatric condition is the proximate agent, and the single largest located cohort reports overlapping error bars across all nine therapies alongside differential surveillance intensity.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of hypothyroidism is established for any individual: the located anchors are cohort designs in which the exposure is prescribed lithium rather than the psychiatric condition itself, the US competing-risk anchor reports that lithium was not statistically significantly different from quetiapine and that error bars overlapped for all nine therapies, that same anchor documents 2.26 to 3.05-fold greater hypothyroidism testing on lithium which inflates measured incidence, the Oxford anchor shows the effect is specific to hypothyroidism with hyperthyroidism and adjusted-calcium outcomes null, and bipolar disorder carries its own independent thyroid autoimmunity signal so disease and treatment cannot be separated within these designs; individual claims require dated lithium start, stop, dose, and serum-level history with dated thyroid studies before and after initiation, a documented lithium-free or alternative-mood-stabiliser interval where one exists, and exclusion of autoimmune thyroiditis, iodine exposure, prior thyroid radioiodine or surgery, pituitary disease, and non-prescribed lithium sources.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Lithium concentrates in the thyroid, impairs hormone release and synthesis, and inhibits thyroid hormone signalling at the level of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis, producing a dose-dependent fall in free thyroxine with a compensatory rise in thyroid-stimulating hormone; the route the dose-response gradients quantify directly, with serum-level thresholds identified for the thyroid outcomes and with women under 60 and above-median concentrations at greatest risk, but whether the prescription produced any individual's hypothyroidism independently of bipolar disorder's own thyroid autoimmunity remains hypothesized until the pre-treatment and post-treatment thyroid function are read against the medication timeline.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at population-register, thirty-year-laboratory-retrospective, and national-claims-competing-risk class following the file's existing treatment-mediated convention (the registered bipolar-disorder to anxiety-disorder edge at PHARMACOLOGICAL_IATROGENIC) and the treatment-mediated precedent class (polymyalgia-rheumatica to osteoporosis at glucocorticoid burden and renal-toxicity to chronic-kidney-disease at toxic exposure): the Hong Kong register anchor is the largest located population with incident bipolar disorder and supplies the active-comparator structure, the dose-response gradient, and derived serum-level thresholds, and additionally reports a NULL for stage 4 or higher chronic kidney disease and end-stage kidney disease despite a stage 3 signal, which is carried openly (PMID 39932712); the Oxford laboratory anchor supplies a three-decade adjusted hazard ratio of 2.31 with specificity for hypothyroidism over hyperthyroidism and with a sex and age risk gradient (PMID 26003379); and the US competing-risk anchor is deliberately registered as the counterweight rather than as support, because it is the anchor that reports overlapping error bars across all nine therapies, no statistical difference from quetiapine, and differential surveillance intensity favouring detection on lithium (PMID 27226264); because the exposure throughout is the prescribed medication rather than the psychiatric condition, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, names lithium as the proximate agent in the mechanism and the alternatives, and routes individual claims through a medication timeline that can be separated from disease-associated thyroid autoimmunity.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are observational and cannot exclude bipolar disorder's own thyroid autoimmunity as a contributor, because no anchor compares lithium-treated against untreated bipolar patients; the largest anchor reports a null for stage 4 or higher chronic kidney disease and end-stage kidney disease despite a stage 3 signal, so the renal consequence is bounded and the hypothyroidism consequence is not; the US competing-risk anchor reports overlapping confidence intervals across all nine therapies, no statistical difference between lithium and quetiapine, and 2.26- to 3.05-fold greater hypothyroidism testing on lithium, so its hypothyroidism incidence estimate is detection-inflated even though the comparative ranking is informative; no located anchor reports a lithium-free control arm drawn from the same bipolar population; the older prevalence estimate of 10.4 percent overall with 14 percent in women against 4.5 percent in men (PMID 10789300) and the graded thyroid-stimulating-hormone rise by lithium band (PMID 37704933) were located and reviewed but are not among this edge's three registered references because the larger contemporary designs supersede them.
